content.text:
I need help rewriting the About page for our company and I think the current version is the problem, not the product. Let me give you the background first and then paste what we have.

We sell scheduling software to independent restaurants. Most of our customers are owner-operators with between one and four locations, and the person who actually buys the thing is usually the owner, who is also often the person doing the schedule at eleven at night on a laptop in the back office. They are not buying software because they love software. They are buying it because they lost a Sunday to a spreadsheet and a chain of text messages about who is covering the brunch shift.

The page we have now was written by an agency two years ago when we were trying to sell to restaurant groups with fifty locations, and that market never worked out for us. So the copy talks about enterprise deployment and multi-region rollouts and it opens with a sentence about how we were founded by two brothers who wanted to change the way the world works. Nobody who reads that page is a fifty-location group anymore. They are one guy with a bar and a wine list.

What I want is a page that a busy owner would read the first two sentences of and think, these people have met a restaurant. It should be short. It should not have a mission statement. It can mention the founders but only if it says something a customer would care about, and honestly I am not sure the founder story earns its space at all.

The constraint from our side is that the legal team will not let us say anything about time saved unless we can point to a study, and we do not have one, so no percentages and no claims about hours back per week. We can say what the software does and we can describe the situation the customer is in.

Can you draft two versions, one that keeps a short founder paragraph and one that drops it entirely, so I can put both in front of the team and let them argue about it.
